Sara —

Thanks — attached is a concise MAP and the summary of our quantization/kernel profiling runs. High level summary up front so your procurement folks can read the one-pager:

- Baseline (FP16/BF16): p50 TTFT 95ms, p95 TTFT 210ms, steady-state throughput ~12k tokens/sec per instance at concurrency 8.
- INT8 (quantized weights + activation calibration): p50 TTFT 105ms (+10%), p95 TTFT 240ms (+14%), throughput ~14k tok/sec (+16%), unit-cost reduction ~32%. No significant quality regressions on our 2k-eval set (ROUGE/EM within 1.5%).
- INT4 (aggressive quantization): p50 TTFT 130ms (+37%), p95 TTFT 330ms (+57%), throughput ~16k tok/sec (+33%), unit-cost reduction ~48%. Observed a 4.8% increase in semantic regression on long-form summarization evals at sequence lengths >2k tokens; flagged for canary-only usage.

Attached: perf_summary_q3_2026.xlsx and kernel_profiles_INT8_INT4_20260814.pdf.

Proposed MAP (milestones):
1) Agreement on target SLOs and acceptable quality delta — owner: Sara / Acme (due Aug 3).
2) Production-like canary (INT8) for 48 hours against 10% of traffic — owner: Jordan / Redwood (due Aug 10).
3) Quality regression check and threshold gating (automated evals) — owner: Marissa (due Aug 12).
4) Contract signature & PO (expected) — owner: Sara/Acme procurement (target Aug 31).
5) Full cutover and dedicated pool activation — owner: Karthik (target Sep 7).

If that aligns, we can update HubSpot with the MAP and lock dates.

-Jordan
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Li <tom.li@foundrycloud.com>, Sara Vance <sara@acme.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-05T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance checklist before procurement

Tom —

Good question. Short answers and data points from the kernel profiling run (see attached PDF for traces):
- Batching policy: continuous batching with per-model max batch 64, dynamic latency target 200ms. Typical effective batch sizes during steady-state: 10-18 tokens/batch for our request mix.
- Max concurrent requests per GPU during tests: 32 logical concurrency (we used 8 worker threads x 4 model shards).
- p95 at concurrency 32:
  - FP16 baseline: p95 TTFT 430ms
  - INT8: p95 TTFT 510ms (about +18%) — observed small increases in kernel scheduling overhead under high concurrency.
  - INT4: p95 TTFT 710ms (+65%) — pronounced tail in long-sequence windows, linked to mixed-precision fallback paths in two attention kernels.

Kernel profile notes: INT8 has favorable compute/memory tradeoffs with a few kernels (matmul and RMS-norm) seeing 1.5-2x speedups. INT4 increases packing/unpacking overhead and triggers a small number of slower fallback kernels on sequences >1024 tokens. We recommend INT8 as the primary quantized offering; INT4 for batch offline/low-SLO workloads or gated canaries.

We'll include suggested autoscaler steps for FoundryCloud in the MAP doc.

-Karthik
Sr. Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Sara Vance <sara@acme.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-12T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance checklist before procurement — Eval results and gating

Sara —

We finished the automated regression checks against Acme's seed eval set (2,032 items, mixture of short Q&A, multi-turn, and long-form summarization). Highlights:
- INT8: quality delta vs FP16 baseline: BLEU/ROUGE/ExactMatch changes all within +/-1.5%; pass threshold defined in MAP is 2.5% — PASS.
- INT4: failed at long-form summarization slice: mean semantic similarity drop of 4.8% (fail threshold 3%). Also saw generation truncation incidents at sequence lengths >2.5k where token packing exceeded the optimized kernel path.

Recommendation: gate INT8 for canary at 10% traffic with automatic rollback on >2% quality regression or >5% error rate increase. Block INT4 for production for now; allow private canaries (offline batch) for cost analysis and longer-term kernel work.

I'll push the detailed gating rules to the MAP doc and create the acceptance webhook for your QA automation.

-Marissa
Lead Applied ML, Redwood Inference
